div.head: ECf 35
div.ab: Iste supradictus Eadmundus habuit filium quendam, qui uocatus est Eadwardus. Qui, mortuo†† patre, timore regis Cnuti aufugit de ista terra usque ad terram Rugorum, quam nos uocamus Russeiam. Quem rex ipsius terre, Malesclodus nomine, ut audiuit et intellexit, quis et unde esset, honeste retinuit eum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 664 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann prints his note letter a before “Iste”, level with the heading of ECf retr 35, to which his note a refers.
There is no note 13 in the ECf column of this page: Liebermann’s numbering goes from 12 to 14.
Liebermann prints “mortuo††” and gives in the outer margin of the ECf retr column the date ††1016.
The starred notes (*, **, ***) are printed across the whole page; they are given with both columns.

note.seg: falls in der Überschrift des Retr. Dauid ursprünglich fehlte, so meinte sie unter Margaretens Söhnen die regierenden Könige von Schottland [oder den gegenwärtigen] und entstand, da deren letzter, David, 1153 starb, vor 1153

if Dauid was originally lacking in the Retr.’s heading, then the heading meant, among Margaret’s sons, the reigning kings of Scotland [or the present one], and it was written before 1153, since the last of them, David, died in 1153

div.ab: This Edmund mentioned above had a certain son, who was called Edward. He, when his father was dead††, for fear of King Cnut fled from this land to the land of the Rugians, which we call Russia. When the king of that land, Malesclodus by name, heard and understood who he was and whence, he kept him honourably.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Eadmund II.; Kiew. Jaroslaw I. war Schwiegersohn Olafs von Schweden. Er sandte die Agsächs. Prinzen nach Ungarn. Die Russische Dynastie verband sich damals nord. und westl. Fürsten (z. B. Gytha, Tochter Harolds II.) und beherbergte solche als Flüchtlinge; vgl., auch über die Namen (Bufleselot), Ediger Russlands ält. Bez. zu Deutschl. (Diss. Halle 1911) 32. 35. 67. 109. 113. — Rugi heissen die Russen bei Franzosen z. B. Bouquet XI 48 — Überschrift9—14 fehlt — Iste p. (ohne uero15) Ea. Ireneside — terre illius (besser laut ECf) Malesclotus23 Rs

Cf. Gl Eadmund II.; Kiew. Yaroslav I was son-in-law of Olaf of Sweden. He sent the Anglo-Saxon princes to Hungary. The Russian dynasty at that time allied itself with northern and western princes (e.g. Gytha, daughter of Harold II) and harboured such as refugees; cf., also on the names (Bufleselot), Ediger Russlands ält. Bez. zu Deutschl. (Diss. Halle 1911) 32. 35. 67. 109. 113. — The Russians are called Rugi by Frenchmen, e.g. Bouquet XI 48 — heading9—14 lacking — Iste p. (without uero15) Ea. Ireneside — terre illius (better, according to ECf) Malesclotus23 Rs
